title: State of Haryana v. Rampal Das @ Sant Rampal (Satlok Ashram Siege)
crime_type: Armed Siege Against State Forces / Sedition / Private Militia Hostage Fortification
court_or_authority: Additional District & Sessions Court, Hisar / High Court of Punjab & Haryana
source: Punjab & Haryana High Court Judgment & Indian Kanoon
ipc_sections: Section 121 IPC (Waging war against the Government of India)
location: Satlok Ashram, Barwala, Hisar, Haryana, India
evidence: Fortified 12-acre ashram compound with watchtowers, razor wire barricades, petrol bomb stockpiles, and acid containers
Seizure of 3 single-barrel rifles, 18 double-barrel guns, 2 revolver firearms, and 500 rounds of live ammunition from sanctum sanctorum
Detention of over 15,000 women and children kept as human shields to prevent security force water cannon and tear gas advance
Autopsies confirming five women and an infant died of asphyxiation and dehydration due to forced confinement inside compound
modus_operandi: Self-styled religious preacher defied 43 non-bailable arrest warrants issued by the High Court. Raised a trained private militia (Rashtriya Samaj Seva Samiti) equipped with batons, firearms, and acid pouches. Fortified ashram compound, using thousands of followers (including women and infants) as human shields against state police and paramilitary personnel during a two-week siege.
personality_disorder: Megalomanic religious cult delusions, defiance of constitutional judicial authority, and militarized authoritarian control.
common_traits: Religious cult compound fortification with private armed militia
Holding followers as captive human shields against police forces
Discharging acid bombs and live ammunition from compound watchtowers
Sedition and systematic contempt of high court warrants
summary: One of the largest domestic police siege operations in modern Indian history, costing over ₹26 crore to enforce court warrants. The Hisar Sessions Court convicted Rampal and 14 followers to life imprisonment for murder and criminal conspiracy.
